No-finding. At 2884188263f3dad5753da7b2e507f6ba55e30eb0 the CSV and calendar actions fail closed, then a later attempt can succeed. No product patch.

The commit message itself was not retrieved. These files did download from that revision:

File	SHA256
hosted/app/phone/PhoneApp.tsx	cea98d8442f0dcb43cee2b1e3d5d5a2814a89130b7c18793ee50f4a8366d5368
hosted/app/phone/record-tools.ts	910dae464cd8504ed225fe5f68fa6b0750c7b7a9c7b18c6454ff4504a772e9a9

record-tools.ts is the same bytes as the earlier CSV/ICS check. The spreadsheet disclosure already tells people to import quoted fields as text. The calendar disclosure already says a later date change does not update an imported event, and that the private note is not in the file.

Node v24.22.3 ran the existing hosted/tests/phone-record-tools.mjs against this PhoneApp.tsx: 31 passed, 0 failed, about 2.0 seconds. That includes the guest and signed-in CSV action, the lock, identity, owner, and workspace rejections, and the calendar recheck after the hash.

The production run, download, exportRecordsCSV, and exportFollowUp functions were then executed with a recording port, not a browser. Saved data was not written. No network call was made.

No records: error “Save an application record before exporting a spreadsheet.” No download. Adding a record then downloads.
createObjectURL throwing: error notice, snapshot unchanged, busy cleared, next attempt downloads.
A NUL title fails schema validation before a file is created. The notice is the normal verification sentence. Restoring the title downloads.
A second calendar request while the first is still hashing does not download. After it finishes, another request does.
Filenames stay Career-Finder-application-records.csv and Career-Finder-follow-up.ics even when the title contains Arabic text, a newline, and ../../. The CSV blob begins EF BB BF. Its type is text/csv;charset=utf-8. The profile name is absent and the private note is present. The calendar type is text/calendar;charset=utf-8 and the note is absent.

Forcing click() to throw also recovers the notice and the next download, but that port left the temporary link attached and did not revoke the blob URL. A normal browser click does not throw, and revoking immediately on the success path would be the wrong change. That is not a patch.

Smallest browser check, for the owner’s real download pass: save one synthetic record with an Arabic title and a private note, export the CSV twice, then download the follow-up file, change the date, and download again. Expect those two fixed filenames, the note only in the CSV, and no change to an event already imported. With the account lock showing, both buttons stay disabled and no file appears. A success notice only means the click was issued."}

Source applicability is approved for the publisher's stronger hunk. It is not native acceptance, and it does not replace the earlier one-line confirmation.

Against 2884188263f3dad5753da7b2e507f6ba55e30eb0, both sentences are the settled complete-empty copy and no other branch:

Title, only when not searching and pageStatus == "complete": No matching jobs in these boards. (CareerDiscovery.swift:112).
Detail, only for that same status: Try a broader job title, another location, or a different employer board. (CareerDiscovery.swift:121).

emptyState puts those two Text values in one element. The magnifying-glass image is accessibilityHidden(true). The stack uses accessibilityElement(children: .combine) and then accessibilityIdentifier("discovery.empty") (NativeDiscoveryViews.swift:170–177). The test resolves that identifier (CareerFinderUITests.swift:227–228). The hint is therefore part of empty.label, not a separate element. contains does not depend on the join separator.

The fixture makes that pair specific. "nothing matches" matches neither synthetic title, remoteOnly defaults to false, and the returned page is status: "complete" with zero jobs (CareerAppEnvironment.swift:139–147). execute stores that page, replaces jobs, and clears isSearching in the same success path (CareerDiscovery.swift:570–571). displayedEmptyStatus then returns "complete". The partial, unavailable, fresh-start, and unknown-status strings are different sentences, so neither check accepts those states.

testSearchEmptyAndFailurePreservesPreviousResults uses launch() with -AppleLanguages (en) and -AppleLocale en_US. English l10n returns the source string unchanged (NativeLocalization.swift:132–133). The Arabic catalog is not on this path.

No source mismatch found. a17999ce was not on the remote, so this is a review of the pasted hunk against those 288 files. No UI test was run."}

Career Finder — Free-Cost Blocker Remedies and Competitive Acceptance Evidence
Heavy session. Access date: 18 November 2026. Latest source: publisher 2884188263f3dad5753da7b2e507f6ba55e30eb0 (merging root9d + search0be). CI 44185640786: service/Android/unsigned-iPhone pass, audit fails, iPhone 16/17 has source-confirmed stale completed-empty expected string (publisher/Build2 own review; no duplicate native fix). Root owns account/browser and actual export-consumer review. Recovery and accessibility terminals retain their work. Development 5bc owns production picomatch remedy. No source edits, native builds, CI runs, applications, account actions, dependency installs, or expensive probes. Original cutoff 18 Nov 22:26:12 UTC unchanged. Good Spender excluded. No universal superiority claim. No new unapproved cost; feasibility, scope and privacy assessed separately.

1. Picomatch Advisory and PR 257 (Source Inspection Only)

Confirmed source (GitHub Advisory, still active):

github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf
High, GitHub Reviewed, affected <= 4.0.7, patched versions none. Locked tree still contains 2.3.2 / 4.0.4 / 4.0.7.

PR 257 inspection (open, head 4e4892e0ac6c374ec3d9e4dc430101da9a20a37b):

github.com/micromatch/picomatch/pull/257

Title: “fix: drop redundant repetition from star-led repeated extglobs”.
Approach: isStarLedBranch + analyzeRepeatedExtglob detects when every branch is star-led and cannot match /. Returns { risky: false, redundantRepeat: true }. Remaps closing: + → @, * → ?.
Excerpt (from files): “When every branch is star-led the repetition is redundant, so +(...) can close like @(...) and *(...) like ?(...) without changing what the pattern matches.”
Example claimed: +(*a) changes from (?:[^/]*?a)+ to (?:[^/]*?a).
No caller-option or capture:true changes visible in the inspected diff.
Excluded: branches that can match / (e.g. +(*/a)), mixed branches (+(*a|b)), patterns disabled by { maxExtglobRecursion: false }, and +(?*a) (noted as related bug).
Author reports differential fuzzing (26.8 M comparisons, 0 divergences) and full suite pass. These are author counts, not independently verified here.
Status: open. Not a released fix.

Comparison to prior open PRs (no executions):

PR 237 (1bf0d045…): collapses self-repeating star branch; contains exact positive assert(isMatch('abc', '+(*)c')); has unsafe inline timing probe.
PR 246 (f03bec2c…): narrower grammar; under capture: true falls back to literalization and deliberately changes capture-mode matches.
Residual v2 capture:true timeout previously preserved: PR 257 does not address it; no change to capture semantics observed.

Distinctions (source-bound):

Released fix: none.
Open proposal: PR 257 (and 237/246).
Source repair: would require the vulnerable path in lib/parse.js to be removed or rewritten on the exact resolved versions.
Actual exposure: still present in locked 2.3.2/4.0.4/4.0.7; reachability in minified build not proven.
Scanner policy: GitHub Reviewed High remains; a renamed fork or same-version patch can leave the entry flagged.

Falsifying cases (proposed, not run):

+(*a) on short adversarial input still exhibits exponential time after applying the PR 257 patch.
isMatch('abc', '+(*)c') (or equivalent capture consumer) returns false under the options used by vite/micromatch/tinyglobby.
Mixed branch +(*a|b) remains exponential (already noted as limitation).
Audit still flags after a local same-version patch that keeps the package version.

Development 5bc owns any production remedy. No audit suppression recommended. No claim that PR 257 is sufficient.

2. CSV / ICS / Native JSON Consumer Acceptance Contract (Official Sources)

CSV (RFC 4180, Informational):

rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180

CRLF record separators; fields containing comma, quote or line-break must be quoted; embedded quote doubled.
Charset is a MIME parameter; file-on-disk has no mandatory encoding. UTF-8 is common practice, not required by the RFC.
LibreOffice Calc CSV filter (help / filter options): “Evaluate formulas” token controls whether leading = is treated as formula or text. Default behavior can evaluate. BOM inclusion is an export option. Encoding detection can fail (UTF-8 read as Latin-1 produces mojibake).
Expectation for root’s consumer tests: quoted fields with Arabic, commas, newlines and leading formula characters remain literal text when imported with “Evaluate formulas” off and UTF-8 selected. Formula prefixing (if used) must be disclosed. No claim of universal spreadsheet safety. Privacy: credentials, tokens and CV bytes must be omitted.

ICS (RFC 5545 §3.3.4 DATE):

rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545

DATE = YYYYMMDD (no separators, no time). Used for all-day / civil dates.
For VEVENT with DTSTART;VALUE=DATE and no DTEND/DURATION, duration is one day. DTEND (if present) is exclusive.
Expectation: single civil follow-up date exported as DTSTART;VALUE=DATE (and DTEND the next day if present) must import as an all-day event on the same civil date in Apple Calendar and other RFC-compliant clients, without timezone shift. Repeated import of the same UID should not create duplicates if the client honors UID. Date change in the source record requires a new export. No claim of every client’s behavior.

Native JSON (phone-workspace import/export):
Build2 has already verified schemas and produced distinct-draft fixtures. Expectation for root: round-trip preserves user notes, stages and canonical job identity; does not invent employer confirmation; omits credentials. Platform scope is native only.

Root owns actual export-consumer review. These are precise expectations, not fabricated passes.

3. Narrowly Scoped Free-Cost Improvements (Existing Features Not Relabeled as Missing)

Existing Saved-note search, CSV, single-date ICS and partial-source hand-off are already implemented or assigned. The items below are additional bounded continuations feasible with current free infrastructure and existing owners. No new unapproved cost.

Partial + board hand-off discoverability on integrating checkpoint
Current source evidence: discovery already retains validated prefix and exposes boardUrl.
Value: user sees a usable employer page when API is partial/stale.
Minimal test: fixture shows retained jobs + board link; no completeness claim.
Costs/permissions: none.
How advantage fails: competitor clipper captures the same posting in one click with richer metadata.
Owner: search terminal.

Native JSON round-trip consumer verification
Current source evidence: phone-workspace JSON import/export exists; Build2 verified schemas.
Value: user can move unfinished drafts between devices without loss.
Minimal test: distinct-draft fixture round-trips with notes/stages intact.
Costs/permissions: none.
How advantage fails: competitor cloud sync is automatic and conflict-resolved.
Owner: recovery terminal + root.

Physical AT on partial/status paths
Current source evidence: polite status pattern already preferred; prior large-text issues observed.
Value: user with VoiceOver/TalkBack can complete search and save without focus theft.
Minimal test: physical AT on integrating checkpoint for partial notice and save.
Costs/permissions: none.
How advantage fails: competitor mobile apps already pass physical AT on their critical paths.
Owner: accessibility terminal under root coordination.

Old native title/date ranking visibility
Current source evidence: older lead feed contains title/date ranking and dated assessments.
Value: user sees chronological or title-sorted results without a new matching model.
Minimal test: confirm ranking still present and not overwritten by newer discovery surface.
Costs/permissions: none.
How advantage fails: competitor relevance ranking (even free tier) surfaces better matches for the same query.
Owner: search terminal.

Privacy declaration accuracy for existing export
Current source evidence: CSV/ICS omit credentials by design; privacy policy URL still required for store.
Value: user and store reviewer see truthful data handling.
Minimal test: signed build in-app deletion + live privacy policy matching actual flows.
Costs/permissions: none beyond existing publisher work.
How advantage fails: competitor privacy docs already describe Gmail/Calendar signals with explicit user approval.
Owner: publisher + root.

Research finished. Available for the next evidence-based question. Heavy session remains Heavy."}
